mappings.note: Names the Hindi word for a weekly or neighbourhood market. LO-252 is the outcome about how local markets work, which is where the vocabulary of the local haat belongs.
Buyers and sellers meeting virtually against meeting in person. A distinction between market types, so the economics goal rather than the local-market outcome.
An overpriced lot of guavas failing to sell. The price mechanism, so CG-SST4.
Wholesalers buying in bulk from producers and selling to retailers. The supply chain under the goal.
Cold storage for perishables. Market infrastructure under the goal.
End-of-season discounting on sweaters explained as clearing stock when demand falls. A pricing strategy, so CG-SST4; not LO-252, since no market is being observed.
The retailer's place in the market chain. The supply chain under the goal.
Asks for the features of a market and then for what the learner actually noticed on a recent visit. That is the field-observation outcome in its own words.
Discusses the economist's epigraph against the chapter's account of markets. Economic reasoning under the goal.
A school carnival's stalls, selling and bargaining, investigated by talking to friends and teachers. A first-hand enquiry into how a market works, so LO-252.
Checking five products for certification marks and asking why some lack them. Consumer protection and standards, so the goal; the enquiry is into products rather than into a market's working.
Designing a label and deciding what a consumer needs to know. Product information and consumer interest under the goal. Not LO-251: a label is mandatory information, not advertising.
Defines a market as the meeting of buyers and sellers. The chapter's founding concept under the goal.
Hampi Bazaar placed in the Vijayanagara empire. A historical market, so the history goal rather than the economics one.
Domingos Paes's account of Hampi as the best-provided city. A foreign traveller's account used as evidence, which is the history goal's sources clause.
Defines price in a transaction. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Inputs for production - the resources a producer buys. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
A government-set minimum price assuring farmers of a floor. The role of government in the economy, which the goal names.
Price ceilings on lifesaving drugs to keep them affordable. Government intervention in markets under the goal.
A failed onion crop pushing prices up. Supply and price reasoning under the goal.
Sorts the government's real market roles from a non-role. The role of government in the economy under the goal.
An aggregator app connecting many sellers to many buyers. Modern market institutions under the goal.
Surat as a diamond and textile hub. The geography of markets and industry under the goal; not LO-252, because no local market is being examined first-hand.
Matches market types to their defining features. A classification of markets under the goal.
Markets letting people obtain what they cannot produce themselves. The socio-economic role of the market, stated almost in the goal's own terms.
Finds the wrongly defined market term among export, import, domestic and wholesale. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Rejects the claim that Hampi traded only local crafts, since it drew goods from far away. A historical market read from travellers' accounts, so CG-SST2.
A profitable season leading the farmer to plant more guavas next year. Supply response to price, so CG-SST4.
Matches six market types to their criteria. A classification of markets under the goal.
Why some goods stay dear although few people buy them - scarcity, brand, cost. Price reasoning beyond simple demand, so CG-SST4.

A real cart-versus-super-bazaar episode, with bargaining refused and a higher price paid for packaged beans, used to draw out the non-price factors in buying. That is the working of local markets and shopping complexes, which LO-252 names.
A tomato glut, farmers dumping produce, and what wholesalers and storage could do. Market structure and the supply chain under the goal.
Defines public goods. The government's economic role under the goal.
AGMARK for agricultural produce against ISI for manufactured goods. Quality standards and consumer protection under the goal.
Matches quality marks to what they certify. Standards and consumer protection under the goal.
Why governments impose quality standards and price controls - protecting consumers and fair practice. The role of government in the economy under the goal.
Finds the market participant wrongly matched to their role. The supply chain under the goal.
Rejects the claim that online markets do away with physical goods, with a stray fragment about energy ratings appended. Market types and standards under the goal.
Exports leaving the country against imports coming in. International trade under the goal.
Picks the correctly defined market term. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
